mechanism_narrative: The observed two-week upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility, from -13.3% to -9.7%, indicates a sustained recovery in consumer activity, which will continue to drive retail and recreation visits higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The recent significant increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, from -0.3% to 2.1% in the last week, moving into positive territory, suggests a broader return of essential errands and increased comfort with public spaces, which will spill over to non-essential retail within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 0% change from baseline in the current week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not show an increase in its weekly mean over the next two weeks following GROCERY_PHARM crossing the 0% threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A strong recovery in PARKS mobility, from -28.7% to -6.0% over three weeks, combined with a sustained decrease in RESIDENTIAL time, from 6.1% to 4.4%, indicates that people are increasingly leaving their homes for leisure and outdoor activities, creating a positive spillover effect for nearby retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases while PARKS mobility continues its upward trend and RESIDENTIAL mobility continues its downward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The stabilization of WORKPLACES mobility at approximately -8% from baseline over the last two weeks suggests a baseline of economic activity has been re-established, providing a stable foundation for a gradual increase in associated retail and recreation over the next four weeks, assuming no new restrictions.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES change from baseline remains between -10% and -5% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES remaining stable within the specified range and no new explicit restrictions are imposed.

mechanism_narrative: As TRANSIT mobility continues its upward trend, from -36.6% to -31.7% over three weeks, and approaches -30% from baseline, it signals a critical mass of people returning to public transport, which will facilitate increased access to and visits for retail and recreation within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -30% change from baseline in the next week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week immediately following TRANSIT mobility rising above -30%.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of decreasing RESIDENTIAL time (from 6.1% to 4.4%) and increasing GROCERY_PHARM visits (from -0.3% to 2.1%) indicates a general shift towards more time spent outside the home for essential activities, which will free up time and willingness for non-essential retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or stagnates over the next two weeks despite RESIDENTIAL time decreasing and GROCERY_PHARM visits increasing.

mechanism_narrative: The strong and consistent recovery in PARKS mobility, from -28.7% to -6.0% over the last three weeks, suggests a growing public confidence in outdoor activities and public spaces, which will translate into increased footfall for retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility continues to rise or remains stable above -10% but RETAIL_REC shows a sustained decline over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The broad upward trend across multiple mobility categories (RETAIL_REC, PARKS, TRANSIT) indicates a general easing of unstated or implicit restrictions and a return to pre-lockdown behaviors, which will continue to drive RETAIL_REC upwards over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, while at least two of the specified mobility categories also show a sustained decline.
